BA.rationale: Boeing's fundamental health is severely impaired: the company carries $47B in debt against only $6B equity (debt/equity 7.8x), has generated negative operating cash flow in two of the last three reported quarters, and remains unprofitable on a net income basis despite $22B quarterly revenue. The Q1 2026 results show a near-breakeven net loss of -$7M on $22.2B revenue, but this masks a gross margin of only 11.5% and operating margin of 2.0%, which are structurally thin for a capital-intensive manufacturer. The trajectory is mixed at best: YoY revenue grew 14% but EPS deteriorated 31%, and operating cash flow swung to -$179M from +$227M the prior quarter. Valuation is extreme: P/E of 74.7x on barely positive earnings, P/B of 28.2x on a thin equity base, and P/S of 1.83x — all near the top of their 12-month ranges. The stock has declined 4.3% over the last quarter and sits well below its 52-week high of $254, yet remains expensive on every fundamental metric. Near-term catalysts are negative: 777X certification may be delayed into the late 2020s, 737 MAX production is capped at 42/month by the FAA (below Boeing's 47/month target), supply chain bottlenecks persist, and the DOJ is pursuing criminal charges for breach of the 2021 DPA. The Q2 earnings report on July 28 is expected to show continued losses (-$0.24 EPS consensus).
